subject: Rolling SOC 2 window mismatch & subprocessor evidence request
messages:
From: Lara Gomez <l.gomez@evergreenhealth.org>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evergreen Health Procurement <procurement@evergreenhealth.org>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II coverage: cloud provider rolling window and subprocessor evidence

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking this — we're preparing Evergreen's procurement package and need to confirm a few items before we finalize the security attestation section. A couple of items popped up while reviewing the SOC 2 reports you provided:

1) Rolling audit windows: Redwood's SOC 2 Type II shows an audit window of 2025-08-01 to 2026-01-31, but the cloud provider (AWS) report you referenced appears to have a different 2024-10 to 2025-09 window. Can you confirm how Redwood maps cloud-provider coverage to your corresponding customer-facing window? For procurement we need an explicit statement clarifying whether there is any gap in coverage for services relied upon (particularly S3 backups and KMS key management).

2) Subprocessor effective dates: please provide the authoritative subprocessor list with effective dates (not just current vendor names). Evergreen requires the effective-on dates for each subprocessor so we can confirm whether the SOCs cover those relationships for our contract term (starting 2025-11-01).

3) Bridge letter / carve-out options: if there's an audit-window mismatch, would Redwood obtain a bridge letter from the cloud provider or provide its own carve-out statement confirming scoping and shared responsibility? If you can share a draft of the language you typically provide, that would speed downstream legal review.

4) Evidence for Dedicated deployments: one of our security controls requires evidence that Dedicated customers have network isolation (VPC / dedicated tenancy) and KMS key custody separation. If you have a deployment diagram and a short explanation of how KMS keys are handled for Dedicated vs Hosted APIs, please attach.

We commonly bundle these items into a single packet — subprocessor CSV, deployment diagram, and the bridge-letter draft. Could you get those to us by end of week? If not, a quick sync call would work — our security lead is available Thursday afternoon PST.

Thanks,
Lara

--
Lara Gomez
Senior Security Auditor
Evergreen Health
l.gomez@evergreenhealth.org

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Lara Gomez <l.gomez@evergreenhealth.org>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 12:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: cloud provider rolling window and subprocessor evidence

Hi Lara — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (security) and Mina (infra) to surface the right artifacts. Short answers up front, then next steps:

- Rolling windows: We use customer-facing audit window = Redwood's Type II window (we contractually tie our SOC coverage to that window). When cloud provider reporting windows don't align, we provide either (a) a bridge letter from the cloud provider or (b) a Redwood-provided carve-out statement that explicitly maps which cloud controls are relied on and which controls Redwood is responsible for.

- Subprocessors: attaching a machine-readable CSV with each subprocessor and an "effective_on" column (see attachment Redwood_Subprocessors_2026-01.csv). The CSV includes historical effective dates where available.

- Bridge letter: attaching a short draft we typically propose; Legal will need to sign off but this is what we send to customers as a starting point (proposed-bridge-letter-draft.docx). If Evergreen prefers Redwood to obtain a cloud-provider bridge letter (some customers do), we can request it but timing depends on the cloud provider (usually 2-4 weeks).

- Dedicated evidence: attaching high-level deployment diagram (Redwood_Dedicated_Deployment_Diagram.pdf). Mina, can you add 2–3 sentences about KMS custody and whether keys are exclusive to Dedicated tenants?

Proposed next steps:
1) We provide the attachments now (CSV + diagram + draft).
2) If Evergreen needs provider-signed bridge letter, we'll open that request with AWS/GCP and update you with ETA.
3) If you want a standalone Redwood carve-out statement (we'll draft and legal will approve), we can provide that within 3 business days.

If that works, I'll schedule a short call for Thursday 3pm PST (Marissa/Mina + me).

Best,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Compliance Programs
Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Lara Gomez <l.gomez@evergreenhealth.org>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II coverage: cloud provider rolling window and subprocessor evidence

Thanks Lara — quick clarifications from Security before the call:

- KMS custody: For Hosted API customers keys are managed by Redwood (we use a multi-tenant KMS policy with envelope encryption); for Dedicated customers we offer two options: (1) Redwood-managed keys in a customer-dedicated KMS key (separate key per tenant), or (2) customer-managed keys (BYOK) where the key material resides in the customer's KMS/HSM and Redwood has no access. Mina — please confirm the language below and whether we have an internal tech note to cite.

- Backups / S3: Backups from Hosted customers are retained in a Redwood-managed S3 bucket with lifecycle rules; for Dedicated we can provide confirmation of separate buckets per customer on request. If Evergreen requires S3-level evidence in the bridge letter, suggest we provide explicit language naming the bucket separation and lifecycle policy.

- Bridge-letter phrasing suggestion (single sentence to include): "Redwood Inference confirms that controls relied upon in Redwood's SOC 2 Type II report include those documented in the referenced cloud provider SOC report(s); where cloud provider windows differ from Redwood's audit window, Redwood has evaluated control continuity and (choose one) obtained a provider bridge letter / issued a carve-out statement mapping shared responsibilities."

Rishi — legal should review the docx I attached and confirm final wording. If Evergreen wants a provider-signed bridge letter, we'll start that request after Evergreen confirms the exact controls (S3/KMS/network isolation) you need covered.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Trust

Rishi / Marissa — this is helpful, thank you. Evergreen is happy to accept Redwood's carve-out statement language if it explicitly calls out S3 backups and KMS custody for Dedicated customers. Two asks to close the loop:

1) Please upload a signed PDF of the Redwood carve-out/bridge-letter (docx -> signed PDF) and attach to the DocuSign envelope below so our legal team can get it into procurement. We're OK with Redwood-provided language; a provider bridge letter is only necessary if Redwood cannot provide an explicit mapping.

DocuSign - Evergreen Bridge Upload: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EVG-Bridge-Request-12345

2) Confirm the CSV has effective dates and that S3/KMS lines show whether the control is shared or Redwood-responsibility (we need a column indicating "shared" vs "redwood" vs "provider"). If you can add that column and re-upload, we'll close our side of the security review.

If you can get the signed PDF + updated CSV by Friday EOD PST we'll aim to get this into the final contract. If timing slips, we can accept a 24–48 hour review buffer.

Best,
Lara
